title: 19 March 1962: Live: Kingsway Club, Southport
content:
This was The Beatles’ seventh performance at the Kingsway Club, situated on the Promenade in Southport, Lancashire. The event was unadvertised, as was the group’s engagement at the venue on the previous Monday.

The Beatles played at the Kingsway Club on eight occasions, all in 1962. The other dates were: 22 and 29 January; 5 and 26 February; 5 and 12 March; and 23 July.

Built in 1931, the Kingsway was a popular venue for live acts from the 1960s through to the 1990s, but closed in 2004. It reopened briefly in 2006 but closed for good the following year. On 6 September 2010 the derelict building was destroyed by fire, and two days later the remains of the building were demolished.

Page last updated: 25 January 2024

Also on this day...

  • 1999: Ringo Starr and his All-Starr Band live: Silver Legacy, Reno
  • 1979: Recording: Getting Closer by Wings
  • 1975: Mixing: Rock Show, Love In Song, You Gave Me The Answer, Magneto And Titanium Man, Letting Go by Wings
  • 1973: Television: James Paul McCartney
  • 1972: Mixing: Angela, The Luck Of The Irish, New York City by John Lennon and Yoko Ono
  • 1971: John Lennon, George Harrison and Ringo Starr file appeal against High Court ruling
  • 1965: Filming: Help!, Austria
  • 1964: The Beatles’ first Top Of The Pops appearance
  • 1964: The Beatles are given Variety Club awards
  • 1964: Filming: A Hard Day’s Night
  • 1963: The Beatles live: Regal Cinema, Cambridge
  • 1961: The Beatles live: Casbah Coffee Club, Liverpool
